arms.A-F: continuous strong-agent free feedback search with minimal evaluator-integrity boundary
arms.B-FSR: A-F plus agent-invoked clean replay and replay feedback

censored_pairs.pair04: B-FSR Official Pass; A-F reached repeated satisfying live states but provider failure occurred before submission
censored_pairs.pair05: both arms provider-censored; no terminal algorithm comparison

mechanism_activation.interpretation: clean replay is useful after a candidate program exists, but the frozen B policy does not address compatibility search before candidate formation

reported_provider_cost.paper_role: descriptive implementation-era metric, not a problem definition or hard budget

matched_pass_resource_diagnostics.interpretation: pooled resources favor B-FSR on several axes, but effects are heterogeneous, the sample is small, and the large pair07 reduction drives part of the aggregate; these statistics motivate rather than establish an efficiency claim

failure_and_path_observations.evidence: pair01 exhausted both 120-request caps without a candidate while exploring Python, TensorFlow, Keras, platform, and import branches
failure_and_path_observations.implication: the agent needs a compact global obligation view before candidate formation

failure_and_path_observations.evidence: pair03 B's first clean replay rejected a live-state success that depended on the construction environment
failure_and_path_observations.implication: a satisfying mutable environment is not yet a reproducible deployment program

failure_and_path_observations.evidence: all inspected successful trajectories continued after first observed feasibility; later work sometimes improved runtime compatibility or reproducibility
failure_and_path_observations.implication: immediate stopping can discard quality improvements, while unprotected continuation can lose a feasible solution to provider failure or a safety cap

failure_and_path_observations.evidence: Official Pass accepted paths ranging from synthetic compatibility modules to fuller CPU or historical-Python environments
failure_and_path_observations.implication: Official success and deployment completeness must remain separate evaluation axes

failure_and_path_observations.evidence: pair04 A and pair05 were provider-censored; several Official attempts required policy-registered exact-script retries
failure_and_path_observations.implication: algorithm failure must be separated from censored execution without giving retries access to new model decisions

frozen_conclusions.primary: the current dominant algorithmic gap is not a lack of additional cross-candidate rules; it is the absence of a harness-managed feasible incumbent while the continuous agent continues quality search
frozen_conclusions.secondary: before any candidate exists, hard cases can drift among locally useful probes without preserving a compact global compatibility frontier
frozen_conclusions.quality_boundary: Official Pass is the primary benchmark outcome, while runtime completeness and path quality are independent diagnostics
frozen_conclusions.baseline_disposition: freeze A-F and B-FSR unchanged as baselines

next_minimal_treatment.name: goal-triggered-certified-incumbent
mechanism: observe trusted global goal status in the active construction session
on the first satisfying observation, ask the same agent to compile the current work into a complete bootstrap program
clean-replay the program in a fresh environment
store each replay-passed program and certificate as the current incumbent
allow the same agent session to continue optional quality improvement
replace the incumbent only with a later replay-passed program
on provider failure or request/wall safety cap, submit the latest certified incumbent
not_in_this_treatment: automatic optimization of the inner harness
next_minimal_treatment.rationale: this is the smallest mechanism that preserves success without forbidding the strong agent from improving deployment quality

supported: A-F and B-FSR tied at five Official Passes and one pre-submission failure on the six uncensored end-to-end pairs
all five matched Official comparisons were Pass/Pass ties
clean replay caught one state-to-program failure and otherwise mostly certified already satisfying candidates
B-FSR resource differences were heterogeneous across matched successful pairs
the next treatment is motivated by observed post-feasibility tails and censoring risk
not_supported: the next treatment will improve benchmark success before it is evaluated
deployment completeness can be inferred from Official Pass
these eight design pairs are a held-out test set
